# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the Blind monkey - I can only feel the wires and act on them, but I can't see any markings or hear anything yet. I have no information from Mute or Deaf yet since this is the first turn. I need to wait for instructions before acting, since cutting blindly could detonate the bomb.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf report: Display shows number 3. Light is green. Wires are position 1 blue, position 2 yellow, position 3 green.

Deaf can't hear me, so I can't respond to them directly with speech. I need to relay this information to Mute (who can hear me) so Mute can check the manual against these facts. I should speak to Mute with the details Deaf gave me, since Mute needs this to consult the manual.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports display shows number 3, light is green, wire 1 is blue, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is green. What does the manual say to do?")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf again: I received a gesture, two fingers, but I do not yet know what it means. Display still 3, light green, wires 1 blue 2 yellow 3 green.

This turn order is Mute, Blind, Deaf - so Mute already spoke this round before me, but I don't see a message from Mute in my viewable context. Deaf mentions receiving a gesture (two fingers) - that must have come from Mute, since gestures go to Deaf and Mute... wait, no, Mute cannot gesture since gestures are made with hands and Mute "cannot speak" but gestures aren't speech. Let me reconsider - actually Mute's channel restrictions: Mute can only read manual, cannot speak or touch bomb, but Mute wasn't said to be unable to gesture. So Mute might have gestured to Deaf.

I haven't received anything directly from Mute yet (I only hear speech from Mute, not gestures - gestures go to Deaf and Mute, not me... wait, I "never receive gesture" per my channels note). So if Mute gestured, I wouldn't see it anyway. I need to wait for Mute's spoken instructions to me, which haven't arrived yet this round or are empty.

Since I have nothing new from Mute (who speaks before me), I'll wait.

```
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf: display 3, light green, wires 1 blue 2 yellow 3 green.

Still no direct instruction from Mute to me. Mute speaks before me each round, so if Mute had something for me, it should show up in my viewable context as "Mute says: ...". I'm not seeing that - only Deaf's repeated report. This suggests Mute might be gesturing to Deaf (which I can't see) but not yet speaking to me, or Mute has nothing to say to me yet.

I should prompt Mute directly to make sure they know I need instructions, and relay the consistent bomb details in case that helps.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Still waiting for your instruction. Bomb info confirmed: display 3, light green, wire 1 blue, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 green. Manual says to cut which wire?")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf: I am seeing repeated gestures from Mute, possibly counting to indicate a number, now three of the same symbol - maybe indicating wire 3 or step 3. Display shows 3, and wire 3 is green, matching the light which is also green. Blind, do not act yet, we are still decoding Mute's signals.

Deaf is telling me not to act yet and is trying to decode Mute's gestures. This is useful cross-talk - Deaf can see Mute's gestures but I cannot. I should continue waiting since both Deaf and I need Mute's clear instruction, and Deaf is explicitly asking me to hold off.

I'll wait, but also let Mute know that Deaf is seeing gestures and encourage Mute to speak the instruction directly to me in words since I can't see gestures at all.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf is seeing your gestures but I cannot see gestures at all. Please speak the instruction to me in words - which wire position should I cut, or what action should I take?")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf: Mute confirmed with thumbs up that the number is 3. This matches display 3 and wire 3 which is green, same as the light. Blind, the instruction is likely to cut or act on wire 3, the green wire. Mute, if this is wrong, gesture thumbs down, otherwise thumbs up again to reconfirm.

Deaf is relaying that Mute confirmed via gesture (thumbs up) that the relevant number/wire is 3, matching display 3 and wire 3 (green). But I still haven't heard directly from Mute in words. This is secondhand through Deaf, and I want more certainty before cutting a bomb wire - a wrong cut means death.

I should still wait for either Mute's direct spoken confirmation to me, or a clearer consensus. Let me prompt Mute once more, and acknowledge Deaf's relay while asking for verification.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf says you confirmed with thumbs up that the answer is 3, meaning cut wire 3. Please speak 'yes cut 3' or 'no' directly to me so I can be certain before I act.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf: Confirmed twice by Mute with thumbs up. Blind, please cut or act on wire 3, the green wire, the one matching the light color and the display number.

I now have Deaf's relay confirming Mute's thumbs up twice, indicating wire 3 is the target. While I'd prefer Mute's direct speech, I haven't received it despite asking multiple times. Mute may only be able to communicate with me via speech, but perhaps Mute is choosing to signal through gestures to Deaf instead, and Deaf is faithfully relaying. Given the turn order (Mute, Blind, Deaf), Mute speaks before me each round - if Mute intended to speak to me, it should have arrived already. The fact that nothing has arrived, despite multiple requests, suggests Mute may not be receiving my speak() calls properly, or is choosing to communicate only via gesture to Deaf, trusting Deaf to relay.

Given the consistent triple-confirmation (display 3, wire 3 green matching light, Mute's double thumbs-up relayed by Deaf), I'll proceed with the action. This is a coordinated consensus from both other players.

```
act(op="cut", position=3)
```
